Definition: from ἄγκος (a bend, "ache"); an arm (as curved):--arm.
BiblicalUsage: Simeon takes the child Jesus up in his arms and blesses God, saying his eyes have seen salvation. The word is the bent arm that cradles, the crook of the elbow where a child is held.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for a cradling arm carries no doctrine of its own; its tenderness is Simeon's, that salvation could be held in a man's arms.
RelatedPeople: Simeon; Jesus; Mary, Mother of Jesus
RelatedEvents: The Presentation of Jesus in the Temple
